IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md
reports.content:
# Implementation plan — Restart and Update as separate runner options + per-runner version pinning

## Goal

Replace the ambiguous "reload" affordance on the System Settings › Runners screen with two
separate actions — **Restart** (destructive, confirmed) and **Update** (reinstall to a
different/newer version) — and add per-runner version control: each runner is pinned either
to `Latest` (default) or to one fixed release, with a version-mismatch warning and an
Update button, red when a newer version exists.

Source request: task title + screenshot (`assets/image.png` shows one runner row,
`local-alpha`, with PAUSE / REVOKE / RELOAD buttons, a build line, and a yellow
version-mismatch banner). Binding survey answers: `SURVEY.md` (round 1, all six questions
answered; see §1).

## 1. Binding survey decisions (do not re-litigate)

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| q1 | Restart = reboot the runner on its current version (debug use when a runner looks stuck). Update = reinstall it onto a different/newer version. Two separate buttons; RELOAD goes away as a runner action. |
| q2 | Restart confirmation warns that any work currently running on that runner will be stopped. |
| q3 | Per-runner dropdown: `Latest` plus every released version to pick from. |
| q4 | Mismatch warning appears whenever the runner's version differs from its own setting, whether fixed or `Latest`. |
| q5 | Automatic update happens only for `Latest` runners, and only when the runner next restarts or is idle with no work running (no mid-work interruption). |
| q6 | Red warning when a newer version exists than the one the runner is on; softer colour for other mismatches. |

Notes captured: restart is a debug tool for stuck runners (q1); Latest default per the
original request.

## 2. Current-state map (verified in repo)

- UI: [RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx](/frontend/src/components/settings/RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx) — detail panel with lifecycle controls, `reloadSelected` (re-reads config from backend, §335–358 — this is the "RELOAD" the screenshot shows; it does **not** touch the runner process), `handleUpdateNow` → `api.requestRunnerUpdate` (queues idle-only `requestUpdate`, §654–676).
- Helpers: [runnerConfigHelpers.js](/frontend/src/components/settings/runnerConfigHelpers.js) — `runRunnerAction` (approve/deny/pause/resume/revoke only, §143–150), `canRequestUpdate`/`canRequestRediscovery` (§421–437), `describeRunnerVersion` (§162–168), `describeRunnerBuild` + `runnerBuildWarning` (§735–810, stale-code banner that already says "restart or update it").
- API surface: [frontend/src/services/runners/index.js](/frontend/src/services/runners/index.js) — `requestRunnerUpdate` posts `{ command: 'requestUpdate' }` to `/runners/:id/commands`; no restart endpoint exists.
- Backend: [api/flow/runnerRegistry.js](/api/flow/runnerRegistry.js) — `RUNNER_COMMANDS = ["requestModelRediscovery", "requestUpdate"]` (§179); heartbeat auto-nudge queues `requestUpdate` for runners trailing recommended version, max one pending and daily per runner (Amendment 1 of [ADR 0012](/docs/adr/0012-runner-artifact-update-channel.md)).
- Runner: [runner/daemon.js](/runner/daemon.js) consumes backend-to-runner commands, advertises `SUPPORTED_RUNNER_COMMANDS` in facts; updates apply idle-only via [runner/updates/](/runner/updates/index.js) (download → verify against pinned key → atomic symlink flip, never downgrade). No restart command exists anywhere.
- Update policy source of truth: `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` / `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` env knobs; procedures in [docs/runner-update-runbook.md](/docs/runner-update-runbook.md). ADR 0012 explicitly deferred per-runner pinning ("no per-runner pinning" in survey refinements) — this task reverses that for the *desired-version* directive only (backend still never serves bytes; R05 stands).
- Tests: `frontend/src/components/settings/runnerConfigHelpers.test.js`, `RunnerConfigurationSection.test.jsx`, `api/flow/runnerVersionCompat.test.js`, `runner/updates-*.test.js`, `api/flow/runnerRoutes.test.js`.

## 3. Approach — make the change easy, then make the change

Do the work in this order so each step is independently shippable and the hard
research lands first:

1. **Research spikes first** (Steps 0a–0c): restart mechanism, version-list source, desired-version storage. These answer the only unknowns; everything after is mechanical.
2. **Make the change easy**: extract the runner-action button + status-line block in `RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx` into small components/helpers with unit tests, so adding Restart/Update/version-selector is adding props, not rewriting the panel.
3. **Make the change**: backend `requestRestart` command + desired-version field, runner daemon support, then UI (separate buttons, confirm modal, version dropdown, warning tiers).
4. **Assure it**: unit/integration/e2e per step + docs updates; keep the old behaviour green until the new one lands.

Non-goals: backend serving runner bytes (R05 stands); Windows support; pre-release opt-in; changing 409/minimum-floor semantics; touching pause/resume/revoke.

## 4. Step-by-step plan

### Step 0a — Spike: restart mechanism (do first; biggest unknown)

- Question: what does "reboot the runner on its current version" mean mechanically? Candidates: (a) new `requestRestart` backend-to-runner command consumed by the daemon (graceful: finish-or-kill work, re-exec wrapper `current` without version change); (b) backend kills the runner process remotely (no — backend has no shell on runner hosts); (c) restart = re-register/reboot host service (out of scope).
- Investigate: how the daemon loop in [runner/daemon.js](/runner/daemon.js) consumes `requestUpdate` end-to-end (heartbeat → ack → idle-apply), where a restart hook fits, what "stop running work" means for claimed tasks (requeue vs kill), and how the wrapper (`bin/kainbain-runner`) re-execs `current`.
- Decide: recommended (a) — symmetric with `requestUpdate`, honours the q2 destructive semantics (work is stopped, not drained), keeps backend coordination-only.
- Evidence: spike note (≤1 page) in the task docs folder naming the chosen hook point and the work-stop semantics.

### Step 0b — Spike: version-list + desired-version source of truth

- Questions: where does the per-runner dropdown's release list come from? Where is `desiredVersion` (`latest` | semver) stored?
- Investigate: backend registry record shape + persistence (disk vs memory — note `pendingCommands` are memory-only per `runnerRegistry.js` §160); whether the backend can list GitHub releases server-side or should expose `recommendedVersion` + a cached release index; how `operatorConfig` (already PATCH-able per runner) could carry `desiredVersion` with `latest` default and backfill for old records.
- Recommended direction (to confirm in spike): `desiredVersion` lives in `operatorConfig` (`null`/`"latest"` = Latest, default); dropdown options = cached release list endpoint (newest-first, same 30-entry bound as the runner client) falling back to `{ current, recommended }` when offline; fixed pin = exact semver; runners resolve `latest` → newest compatible release via the existing compat filter.
- Evidence: spike note + decision on storage/endpoint shape before any schema change.

### Step 0c — Spike: idle-only auto-update vs restart-triggered update

- Reconcile q5 ("only when the runner next restarts or is sitting idle") with current behaviour (hourly idle check + 409-triggered + daily auto-nudge for trailers). Decide the exact matrix: Latest+idle → auto; Latest+busy → wait; fixed-pin → never auto (manual Update only); restart of a Latest runner → check-and-update on boot before claiming work.
- Evidence: one truth-table in the spike note; it becomes the acceptance table in §6.

### Step 1 — Test-seam refactor (make the change easy)

- Extract from `RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx`: action-button row (with disabled-reason tooltips), command status-line builder, version/warning banner block into testable units beside `runnerConfigHelpers.js`.
- Add missing unit coverage for current behaviour first (`runRunnerAction` unknown-action null, `canRequestUpdate` gating, `runnerBuildWarning` branches) so refactors are provably safe.
- Gate: `npm run test:unit` + existing `RunnerConfigurationSection.test.jsx` green, no visual change.

### Step 2 — Backend: `requestRestart` command (mirror `requestUpdate`)

- Add `requestRestart` to `RUNNER_COMMANDS` in `api/flow/runnerRegistry.js`, queue/dedupe/cooldown semantics (mirror `requestUpdate`; decide cooldown in Step 0a), `POST /runners/:id/commands { command: 'requestRestart' }` path, `runnerApi.requestRunnerRestart` in `frontend/src/services/runners/index.js`, `runRunnerAction`-adjacent dispatcher entry.
- Gate: `api/flow/runnerRoutes.test.js` + registry unit tests for queue/dedupe.

### Step 3 — Runner daemon: consume `requestRestart`

- Advertise support in `SUPPORTED_RUNNER_COMMANDS`; implement restart: stop in-flight work per Step 0a semantics (heartbeat ack carries what was stopped), re-exec wrapper on the **same** version (no update check interleaved — Restart ≠ Update per q1), re-register.
- Safety: restart never triggers an update on a fixed-pin runner; on a Latest runner it may check-and-update on boot per Step 0c matrix (document which).
- Gate: `runner/daemon.test.js` + idle/busy restart cases; chaos coverage per `docs/manual-testing/09-runner-chaos.md`.

### Step 4 — Backend + registry: `desiredVersion` per runner

- Schema per Step 0b (`operatorConfig.desiredVersion`, default Latest, backfill old/empty → Latest); PATCH validation (exact semver from release list or `latest`); include resolved `desired` + `latest` + release list in `GET /runners` records (or a lightweight releases endpoint); keep env knobs as fleet defaults.
- Decide conflict rule: fixed pin above recommended is allowed (asymmetric updates already accepted per ADR Amendment 1); fixed pin below minimum still 409s (floor unchanged).
- Gate: registry + compat tests (`runnerVersionCompat.test.js`).

### Step 5 — UI: separate Restart / Update, confirm modal, version selector, warning tiers

- Replace RELOAD-as-action with: **Restart** (destructive styling, opens confirm modal with q2 copy: names the runner, warns running work will be stopped, requires explicit confirm; disabled with reason when runner not active/old) and **Update** (queues reinstall to resolved target: fixed pin → that version; Latest → newest compatible; shows target version in tooltip as today).
- Keep config re-read available but demote it (e.g. small refresh icon, not a primary button) so no capability is lost.
- Per-runner version dropdown (`Latest` + releases, default Latest) bound to `desiredVersion` PATCH.
- Warning logic per q4/q6: mismatch(runnerVersion vs resolved desired) → banner + Update button; tier = red when a newer version exists than running (scare), softer otherwise (e.g. pinned older-behind, dev checkout, unknown). Preserve `runnerBuildWarning` sha-mismatch branch or merge it into the same banner (decide in implementation; no double banners).
- Distinguish three states explicitly: update queued/pending, last-update failed (with reason), update available — reusing the existing `commands.pending`/`results` + `updateStatus` plumbing.
- Gate: helper unit tests (warning-tier matrix) + `RunnerConfigurationSection.test.jsx` additions + headless screenshot (`npm run capture:screenshot`) of row states.

### Step 6 — Auto-update behaviour for Latest (q5)

- Implement the Step 0c matrix; default Latest for new runners; no auto-update for fixed pins (manual Update only).
- Gate: daemon update-client tests + heartbeat-nudge tests proving busy runners are never interrupted.

### Step 7 — Docs + runbook

- Update [docs/runner-update-runbook.md](/docs/runner-update-runbook.md) (Restart vs Update, pin procedure, Latest auto behaviour, triage for the new banners), the Runners settings UI copy, and ADR 0012 Amendment 2 (per-runner desired-version reverses the "no per-runner pinning" deferral for selection only).
- Backwards-compat note: old runners (no `requestRestart`, no `desiredVersion`) show disabled buttons + "update the runner to enable this" guidance, mirroring the existing R1 pattern.

## 5. Ordering / dependencies

`0a, 0b, 0c` (any order, all before schema) → `1` → `2 → 3` (backend then daemon; UI Restart in 5 may mock until 3 lands) → `4` → `5` → `6` → `7`. Steps 2–3 and 4 are parallelisable once spikes conclude.

## 6. Acceptance table (from survey; verify every row)

| Runner setting | Runner state | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| any | press Restart | confirm modal (q2 copy) → reboot same version, running work stopped |
| fixed pin = running | — | no warning |
| fixed pin ≠ running | — | softer warning + Update → reinstalls pinned version |
| Latest, running = newest | — | no warning |
| Latest, trailing | idle/restart | auto-updates (q5); banner red until converged (q6) |
| Latest, trailing | busy | red banner + Update button; no interruption |
| any old runner | — | disabled controls + "too old" guidance, never a dead button |

## 7. Assurance plan (how we prove it)

- Unit: `npm run test:unit` — new helper tests (restart dispatcher, desired-version normalisation, warning-tier matrix incl. red-vs-soft), registry queue/dedupe/cooldown tests, daemon command tests.
- Integration: runner update-client + heartbeat suites (`runner/updates-*.test.js`, daemon tests) for idle-only apply, never-downgrade, opt-out ack, fixed-pin-no-auto.
- UI: extend `RunnerConfigurationSection.test.jsx` (two buttons, modal copy, dropdown default Latest, banner tiers); headless capture (`npm run capture:screenshot`) of: clean row, soft mismatch, red newer-available, pending-update, failed-update, confirm modal.
- Manual: runbook triage walkthrough (stale runner, failed update, old runner) + chaos checklist (`docs/manual-testing/09-runner-chaos.md`).
- Docs: runbook + ADR amendment + settings copy reviewed in the same PR; no code lands without its docs row in §6 re-verified.
- Regression: full suite for touched packages; `api/flow/runnerRoutes.test.js` and existing update-channel tests must stay green (old behaviour preserved until new lands).

## 8. Risks

- Restart-during-work data loss → mitigated by q2 confirm copy + ack reporting what was stopped; never auto-restart busy runners.
- Fixed pin below minimum → 409 loop; UI must surface "pin is below fleet minimum" distinctly from "update available".
- Release-list availability offline → dropdown degrades to current+recommended (R03 offline updates keep working).
- Scope creep into serving bytes or changing floors → explicitly out; R05 stands.

reports.name: spike-notes-0a-0c.md
reports.content:
# Spike notes — Steps 0a–0c (restart mechanism, version-list source, auto-update matrix)

Research for task `78e0522a` (Restart/Update split + per-runner version pinning).
Decisions below are as implemented; file/line pointers are to this branch.

## 0a — Restart mechanism

Question: what does "reboot the runner on its current version" mean mechanically?

- Rejected: backend kills the runner remotely (the backend has no shell on
  runner hosts — coordination-only, R05 stands), and host-service reboot
  (out of scope).
- Chosen: a new `requestRestart` backend-to-runner command, symmetric with
  `requestUpdate` (`RUNNER_COMMANDS` in `api/flow/runnerRegistry.js`,
  consumed in `handlePendingCommands` in `runner/daemon.js`, advertised in
  `SUPPORTED_RUNNER_COMMANDS`). It reboots at once — a live execution is
  stopped, never drained (survey q2 destructive semantics); the orphaned
  claim lease expires so the work re-queues exactly like a crash.
- Hook detail found during review: the `kainbain-runner` wrapper only
  re-execs when the `current` symlink target changed (a staged update), so
  a bare `process.exit(0)` would STOP a same-version runner instead of
  rebooting it. The daemon therefore writes a `restart-requested`
  sentinel beside the install root (`requestWrapperRestart` in
  `runner/updates/state.js`) before exiting 0; the wrapper consumes it and
  boots the SAME tree again. Exit 0 + sentinel keeps systemd
  `Restart=on-failure` supervision quiet. A stale sentinel (crash between
  write and exit) causes at most one extra boot. Unwrapped
  (`node main.js`) runners exit without rebooting — documented in
  `docs/runner-update-runbook.md`, same class as staged updates there.
- No update check is interleaved (Restart ≠ Update, survey q1); the ack is
  confirmed with a final heartbeat first so peek-until-ack redelivery
  cannot restart-loop the rebooted runner.

## 0b — Version-list + desired-version source of truth

- `desiredVersion` lives in `operatorConfig` (`'latest'` default,
  backfilled for old state; strict PATCH validation — `latest`/null or a
  parseable version, else 400 `INVALID_DESIRED_VERSION`).
- The Settings dropdown needs no release-catalogue fetch (offline-safe):
  `fleetKnownVersions` in `api/flow/runnerVersionCompat.js` unions every
  runner-reported version with the recommended/minimum knobs, newest-first,
  capped at 30 (same bound as the runner update client). The UI unions
  that with running + recommended + the stored pin so the current
  selection is always renderable.
- The setting rides the heartbeat `update` directive; the daemon reads the
  pin via `pinnedDesiredVersion` (fail-open to latest-tracking on old
  backends/junk). Fixed pins above recommended are allowed; below minimum
  still 409s (floor unchanged) with a distinct "pin cannot clear the
  floor" banner + disabled Update.

## 0c — Idle-only auto-update vs restart-triggered update (truth table)

| Setting | State | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `latest` | idle (incl. after a restart, once idle) | auto-updates (hourly idle check + daily backend nudge); red banner until converged |
| `latest` | busy | red banner + Update button; never interrupted |
| pinned | any | never automatic (no nudges, no idle installs); manual Update installs exactly the pin when newer, fails loud otherwise |
| pinned = running | — | no warning (unless below minimum — the floor always warns red) |

- Backend nudge (`shouldAutoRequestUpdate`) and the daemon idle check
  (`maybeSelfUpdate`, non-force) both gate on latest-only; force paths
  (manual Update, 409 floor) resolve the pin as the check target.
- A restart never installs anything by itself; a Latest runner converges
  at its next idle check after the reboot.

reports.name: pr-review-20261117.md
reports.content:
# PR review — Restart / Update split + per-runner version pinning (2026-11-17)

**Branch evaluated:** `kb/78e0522a-430d-4659-9e2f-7db6444d13f9`, HEAD `072d1267`, diff `origin/main...HEAD`
(22 code files + ADR amendment + runbook + spike notes).
**Method:** read every previous report, read the full diff, then re-verified each
acceptance row against the code and re-ran the suites myself. No servers started,
no code changed (docs-only stage), no live operations touched.

## Acceptance table — every row verified in code and tests

| Plan §6 row | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Restart → confirm modal (q2 copy) → reboot same version, work stopped | PASS | `RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx`: destructive Restart button, `role="alertdialog"` modal naming the runner, "Any work currently running on this runner will be stopped", busy task id shown; daemon `handlePendingCommands` writes `restart-requested` sentinel, confirms ack via heartbeat, `process.exit(0)` — no update check interleaved |
| Fixed pin = running → no warning | PASS | `versionWarningForRunner`: `order === 0 → null` (below-minimum excepted — floor correctly outranks) |
| Fixed pin ≠ running → warning + Update → pinned version | PASS | Pin newer → red `newer-available`, Update installs exactly the pin; pin older → soft mismatch (red only if something even newer exists, per binding q6), Update disabled with `pinBlocksUpdateReason` (channel never downgrades — reasoned, documented) |
| Latest, running = newest → no warning | PASS | `compare(running, recommended) !== -1 → null` |
| Latest, trailing, idle/restart → auto-updates; red banner until converged | PASS | `shouldAutoRequestUpdate` + `maybeSelfUpdate` both gate on latest-only; pinned returns `manual update only` without network; red banner |
| Latest, trailing, busy → red banner + Update; no interruption | PASS | Red banner; Update queues idle-only via existing `handleUpdateNow` path |
| Old runner → disabled controls + "too old" guidance | PASS | `canRequestRestart` gates on advertised `facts.commands`; `commandDisabledReason` names manual update; old runners ignore unknown commands |

## Review questions

- **Achieves the goal?** Yes. Reload-as-action is gone (demoted to a text button, same `data-testid`, still re-reads config); Restart is destructive + confirmed; per-runner Latest/pin dropdown defaults to Latest; mismatch warning + Update button; red tier when newer exists.
- **Followed the plan?** Yes. Spikes 0a–0c landed as `spike-notes-0a-0c.md` with the truth table; backend → daemon → desiredVersion → UI → auto-update → docs order kept. Two documented deviations, both justified: (1) dropdown uses fleet-known versions (`fleetKnownVersions`, offline-safe) instead of a release-catalogue endpoint — survey q3 asked for "every released version", spike 0b records the offline-safe decision; (2) pin-newer-than-running warns red rather than the plan's shorthand "softer" — binding survey q6 ("red when a newer version exists") outranks the plan summary.
- **Code standards?** Yes. MARK/JSDoc headers on all new units, colocated tests, `npm run lint` clean on touched files (0 errors; only the repo's usual `security/detect-object-injection` warnings, and CI lint passed).
- **Easy to modify?** Yes. Pure helpers (`versionWarningForRunner`, `pinBlocksUpdateReason`, `fleetKnownVersions`, `pinnedDesiredVersion`) carry the policy with unit-tested matrices; UI/backend/runner changes are additive.
- **Best practices?** Yes. Fail-closed enqueue (`UNKNOWN_COMMAND`), fail-open reads (junk → `latest`, never stranded), never-downgrade enforced in three layers (UI disable, backend floor, update-client pre-checks), at-most-once delivery (ack-before-exit prevents restart loops), R1 "never a dead button" throughout.
- **Tech debt?** None unnecessary. Three version-compare implementations (backend semver, runner manifest, frontend numeric) is justified — frontend has no semver dep — and documented. The `api/gitGate.test.js` test-only hardening is out of scope but was required to unblock the gate signal (see below); it touches no product code. The known `$INSTALL_ROOT/bin` shim-refresh gap is documented in the upgrade-safety review and degrades to a systemd restart, not a stranded runner.
- **Docs updated?** Yes. ADR 0012 Amendment 2, `docs/runner-update-runbook.md` (Restart vs Update, per-runner setting, restart-loop + pin triage), spike notes, survey, implementation plan.

## Test evidence (run by this review, on HEAD `072d1267`)

- `npm run test:api` (full): **454 files, 7436 passed, 0 failed** — includes the hardened `gitGate.test.js`, which hung the 03:57 gate pre-fix and now passes in the full run too.
- `npm run test:frontend` (full): **357 files, 4839 passed, 0 failed** — includes 72 `RunnerConfigurationSection` tests (restart modal open/cancel/busy-name/too-old, red vs soft tiers, pin-from-dropdown, queued-restart status) and the `domainRegistry` pin fix for `requestRunnerRestart`.
- Full runner suite via `node --test` (exact CI file list): **444 passed, 0 failed** — daemon restart handler, pinned `checkForUpdate` targets, sentinel write/consume, stale-sentinel single boot.
- Previous CI failures are explained, not recurring: run 1 failed on the `domainRegistry` pin (fixed by `c8a34f29`, green since); run 2 failed on the pre-existing `gitGate` flake before the hardening commit `0603447d` existed.

## Gaps / notes (non-blocking)

- No Playwright screenshots: `capture:screenshot` needs a live app URL, and starting one on this host risks the live runners. The jsdom component tests render the real JSX and assert every row state (clean, soft, red, pending, failed, confirm modal), which is the safer equivalent here.
- "New version published" resolves to the fleet `recommendedVersion` knob (plus fleet-known versions for the red tier) — publishing without bumping the knob shows no banner. This matches the system's existing publish mechanism (runbook) and is the only sane reading, but human reviewers should confirm.

reports.content:
# Upgrade-safety review — Restart / Update split + per-runner desiredVersion

**Stage goal:** verify the current change as implemented will not break existing installs on update. If it would, fail the stage (do not fix).

**Branch evaluated:** `kb/78e0522a-430d-4659-9e2f-7db6444d13f9` diff `main...HEAD` (33 files, incl. `api/flow/runnerRegistry.js`, `api/flow/runnerVersionCompat.js`, `runner/daemon.js`, `runner/updates/index.js`, `runner/updates/state.js`, `runner/bin/kainbain-runner`, `frontend/src/components/settings/runnerConfigHelpers.js`, `frontend/src/components/settings/RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx`).

## Method
Read every changed file on `HEAD` against `main`, plus `scripts/lib/runner-install-root.sh`, `scripts/install-local-runner.sh`, `scripts/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.sh`, `scripts/package-runner.mjs`, and the persisted-state loaders (`api/flow/runnerRegistry.js::_loadState`, `runner/updates/state.js::readUpdateState`). Checked both rollout directions: (a) old installs self-updating to the new code, (b) mixed fleet (new backend ↔ old runner, old backend ↔ new runner, new frontend ↔ old backend).

## Backward-compatibility properties verified

### 1. Backend persisted state — additive, lenient load, no version bump
- `RUNNER_STATE_VERSION` stays `3`. `_loadState`/`_persist` call `normalizeOperatorConfig` unconditionally. New field `desiredVersion` defaults to `"latest"` in `defaultOperatorConfig` and is normalized via `normalizeDesiredVersion(raw.desiredVersion ?? "latest")`. Test `old state predating desiredVersion backfills to latest` (`api/flow/runnerRegistry.test.js`) writes a v3 file without the field (operatorConfig `{ displayName: null }`) and asserts both `desiredVersion` and `operatorConfig.desiredVersion` read `"latest"` after load.
- `normalizeDesiredVersion` (`api/flow/runnerVersionCompat.js`) is lenient on STORE: `null`/`undefined`/`""`/`"latest"`(any case) → `"latest"`; version-like strings coerce via `coerceRunnerVersion`; anything else falls back to `"latest"` — never stranded on an undeployable value. Strictness lives only on `PATCH` (`updateConfig` throws `400 INVALID_DESIRED_VERSION` for malformed strings/non-strings), so a hand-edited state file cannot brick the registry.
- `normalizePendingCommands`/`normalizeCommandResults` filter by `RUNNER_COMMANDS.includes(command)`. Upgrading is safe (old entries are a subset of the new three). Downgrading past a queued `requestRestart` drops that one command — at-most-once semantics, not a fleet brick.
- `updateConfig` whitelist adds `"desiredVersion"`; the `next` copy seeds `desiredVersion: current.desiredVersion ?? "latest"` so PATCHes that omit the field (the only shape old frontends send) preserve the setting instead of resetting it.
- `_public` is additive: `desiredVersion`, `availableVersions`, `update.desiredVersion` are new keys; no existing key is renamed/removed. `fleetKnownVersions` is pure, offline-safe (unions runner-reported versions + `recommended`/`minimum` knobs, `coerceRunnerVersion`-filtered, capped 30) and cannot throw on junk records.

### 2. Old runner ↔ new backend
- Old daemon advertises `["requestModelRediscovery","requestUpdate"]` and ignores unknown commands (`handlePendingCommands` `continue`s). New backend's `enqueueCommand` never gates on advertised commands (pre-existing behaviour), but the UI gates on `commands.supported` (`canRequestRestart` in `runnerConfigHelpers.js` requires `requestRestart` in `facts.commands`), so operators see a disabled Restart with "too old — update the Runner" guidance instead of a dead button. A queued `requestRestart` for a pre-feature runner simply sits until TTL (`24h`) and expires as a failed ack — no crash, no workflow interruption, R1 pattern preserved.
- `updateDirectiveFromBeat` on old runners returns only three keys; new directive adds `desiredVersion: null`. Old runners ignore the new field (their `updateDirectiveFromBeat` predates it). Compat-gated selection therefore behaves exactly as before.
- `shouldAutoRequestUpdate` gains `desiredVersion` param gated by `isPinnedDesiredVersion(desiredVersion ?? DESIRED_VERSION_LATEST)`. Old runners have no pin (default `"latest"`), so the daily auto-nudge behaviour is unchanged: at most one pending, daily cooldown, idle-only apply retained.

### 3. New runner ↔ old backend
- `updateDirectiveFromBeat` reads `desiredVersion` via `pick(update.desiredVersion)` → `null` when the backend omits it. `pinnedDesiredVersion` maps `null`/`"latest"`(any case)/`""`/non-string/junk → `null` (fail-open to latest-tracking, today's behaviour). `maybeSelfUpdate` only skips auto-checks when `effectiveTarget` is a valid pinned string, so old-backend runners keep the hourly idle check + 409-triggered path unchanged. Verified by `pinnedDesiredVersion` and `maybeSelfUpdate` unit tests (`runner/daemon.test.js`: `pinnedDesiredVersion({ desiredVersion: "bogus" }) => null`; heartbeat cases carry `desiredVersion: null`).
- `SUPPORTED_RUNNER_COMMANDS` and `support` filtering are additive. An old backend returns `supported` without `requestRestart` (its `RUNNER_COMMANDS` has two entries), so the new frontend renders Restart disabled — never a broken action.

### 4. Runner self-update — default-path unchanged, new path fail-closed and downgrade-proof
- `checkForUpdate` gains `targetVersion = null` default. `checkGithubForUpdate`/`checkMirrorForUpdate`/`checkSingleMirrorManifest` take `targetVersion` through and branch only when truthy; when `null` every pre-filter is the old expression (`isNewerVersion`, `isPrereleaseVersion` skip, compat filter). The pinned pre-checks (`isValidVersion`, `compareVersions` order `-1`/`0`/`null`) short-circuit before any network when `targetVersion` is set, so junk pins fail loud (`ok:false`, reason string) and never install.
- Pinned install constraints: `compareVersions(target, current) === 0` → `ok:true, update:null, reason:"already on pinned"` (no-op); `-1` → `ok:false, reason:"never downgrades"`; `null` → `ok:false, reason:"cannot compare"`. Mirror/GitHub list walks match `compareVersions(tag, target) === 0` only, never a newer substitute. `checkSingleMirrorManifest` requires the served manifest version to equal the pin. These satisfy ADR 0012 "never downgrade" and "verified, compat-filtered" invariants; a pinned runner therefore cannot silently jump over its pin nor strand below the fleet floor (floor still 409s, UI disables Update with `pinBlocksUpdateReason`).
- `maybeSelfUpdate` with a pin and `!force` returns `{ checked:false, reason:"pinned to X: manual update only" }` without touching the network. Manual `requestUpdate` (force) passes the pin through as `targetVersion`. Indistinguishable from the old path when no pin is present.

### 5. Same-tree Restart reboot — sentinel is best-effort; shutdown is not breakage
- New daemon `requestRestart` handler: stage ack → confirm heartbeat (best-effort, warned on failure) → `requestWrapperRestart({ installRoot: installRootFor(config) })` in try/catch (warns `sentinel not written`) → `process.exit(0)`. The `try/catch` + warn makes an unwritable/missing install root degrade to a plain exit, never a crash. An unwrapped `node main.js` host therefore just exits (as documented) instead of erroring.
- Wrapper (`runner/bin/kainbain-runner`) change: only the `AFTER === BEFORE` branch gains `if [ -f "$INSTALL_ROOT/restart-requested" ]; then rm -f …; RESTARTS++; sleep 2; continue; fi`. Normal completion (single-assignment done / idle-out, no sentinel, no `current` flip) still `exit 0`s directly. A staged update still re-execs via the existing `AFTER != BEFORE` branch. Non-zero daemon exits still propagate with no loop. Stale sentinel safety: `rm -f` before re-exec + the shared `RESTARTS > 50` cap guarantees at most one extra boot, never a loop (both covered in `runner/updates-wrapper.test.js`).
- `requestWrapperRestart` creates the install root recursively and writes `{ pid, at }` JSON. It does not touch `update-state.json` (`readUpdateState` still reports `"idle"` in tests), so the failed-boot rollback gate (`bootstrapUpdateState`, `MAX_BOOT_ATTEMPTS = 3`) is unaffected. A sentinel left by a crash between write and exit is consumed by the same restart counter, not by the boot-attempt gate.
- Existing installs self-updating: `applyUpdate` flips `current`/`previous` and leaves `$INSTALL_ROOT/bin/kainbain-runner` as a stable shim copy. The extracted new tree *contains* the sentinel-aware wrapper but the shim is not refreshed by `applyUpdate`. The old shim still re-execs on `current` flips (old update behaviour intact). The sentinel from the new daemon is ignored by the old shim (no match, plain `exit 0`); systemd units in this repo use `Restart=always` (`scripts/install-local-runner.sh`, `startRunner.sh`), so the reboot strength is unchanged. No install is stranded without a running daemon; the worst case is the new Restart feature degrading to a systemd restart until the shim is re-laid by `install-local-runner`/`migrate-runner-to-wrapper` (both already copy `runner/bin/kainbain-runner` to `$INSTALL_ROOT/bin/kainbain-runner`). This is a feature staleness gap, not a break of existing update/heartbeat/dispatch behaviour.

### 6. Frontend / API — dual-read fallbacks, no breaking contract change
- `resolveDesiredVersion` falls back `desiredVersion ?? operatorConfig.desiredVersion ?? update.desiredVersion ?? "latest"`; `normalizeDesiredVersion` trims and case-folds. Old backends return `undefined`/`""` for the new keys, which read `"latest"` — the version selector renders "Latest (recommended)" and `versionWarningForRunner` for a latest-runner compares `compareRunnerVersions(running, recommended)`.
- `versionOptions` unions `selected.availableVersions ?? []`, `recommendedVersion`, `runningVersion`, and the stored pin, then sorts via `compareRunnerVersions(b, a) ?? 0`, so the current selection is always renderable even when the backend list is empty (offline/regression path). `compareRunnerVersions` returns `null` for unparseable inputs and every caller treats `null` as "cannot prove a difference" — warnings stay quiet on junk instead of scaring.
- `Reload` is preserved as a demoted text button (`data-testid=runner-reload-<id>`, `title="Reload configuration from backend"`). *Restart* is a new separate destructive button with `role="alertdialog"` confirmation (`runner-restart-modal-<id>`, names the runner, warns running work will be stopped, shows current task id when busy). Breaking nothing that existed; `reloadSelected` still re-reads config.
- `domainRegistry` and `runnerRequests` add one operation (`requestRunnerRestart`, `POST /runners/:id/commands { command: "requestRestart" }`) and no operation is removed/renamed. The previous CI failures (`api.surface.test.js`, `domainRequests.test.js` pinning exact key lists) were updated to include the new key; the full frontend suite passes on this branch.

### 7. What was *not* changed
- No new required env vars, no config-schema migration, no `RUNNER_STATE_VERSION` bump, no protocol bump (`RUNNER_PROTOCOL = "v1"` unchanged), no `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` / `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` semantics change, no runner-bytes-via-backend (R05 stands; Amendment 2 touches only the *directive*), no Windows/pre-release policy change.
- `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js` is untouched by the branch (`git diff` null) — the only backend file in the diff is `api/flow/runnerRegistry.js` plus compat helpers. `runner/updates/state.js` only adds `RESTART_REQUEST_FILE` + `requestWrapperRestart`; `readUpdateState`/`writeUpdateState`/`acquireUpdateLock`/`bootstrapUpdateState` semantics unchanged.

No clause of the change breaks an existing install on update. Every rollout direction was verified against actual loader/dispatch code and existing tests: old state backfills, old runners ignore or disable the new command, new runners read old directives as latest, pinned installs fail closed without downgrading, and the Restart sentinel degrades to a systemd restart rather than stranding a runner. The sole soft spot — `$INSTALL_ROOT/bin/kainbain-runner` not being refreshed by `applyUpdate` — leaves the reboot strength intact via `Restart=always` and is already the documented shim-refresh path through the installers, not a fleet break.

**Gate check (evidence on this branch):**

reports.content:
# Stage review (PR-review stage, docs-only) — Restart / Update split + per-runner version pinning

**Branch reviewed:** `kb/78e0522a-430d-4659-9e2f-7db6444d13f9`, HEAD `de3b472a` (working tree clean).
**Scope of this stage:** decide whether the change is suitable to integrate. No code was
modified (docs-only stage); no servers were started; the only live-system contact was
read-only `GET /runners` and `GET /status` against the local backend (127.0.0.1:3100).

## Method

1. Read all previous reports in this task folder (implementation plan, survey, spike
   notes, quick-review failure, upgrade-safety review, PR review, human rejection).
2. OCR'd the human-feedback screenshot `assets/19126.png` (Android shot, 2026-11-17
   07:33) with a locally extracted tesseract 5.5 binary (downloaded debs to /tmp, not
   committed). It shows the Runners settings for `local-alpha`: row `v0.1.0 build
   fbcf844` + STALE CODE, buttons `PAUSE REVOKE RESTART Reload`, build line, the
   warning *"This runner was built from fbcf844 but the backend runs 1.0.0-2…"*, and
   the closed selector `Latest (0.1.0)` with hint "Tracks the newest release — …".
3. Read the current diff (`main...HEAD` plus the already-merged runner/backend parts in
   the working tree) end to end for the touched units:
   `frontend/src/components/settings/runnerConfigHelpers.js`,
   `RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx`, `api/flow/runnerVersionCompat.js`,
   `api/flow/runnerRegistry.js`, `runner/daemon.js`.
4. Executed the current helpers directly with the **live** runner record
   (`GET /runners` → `local-alpha`) and the live backend build identity
   (`GET /status` → `build.commit = "1.0.0-28aac94"`, image tag
   `KAINBAIN_IMAGE_TAG=1.0.0-28aac94`).
5. Re-ran the test suites on HEAD.

## Human correction (assets/19126.png) — verified fixed at HEAD

Complaint: *"it's comparing a hash to a build and the latest image seems to not be
flagged as latest in the drop-down".*

- **Hash vs build.** At screenshot time the sha-mismatch warning printed the raw
  backend identity next to the runner hash (`fbcf844` vs `1.0.0-28aac94` — a
  version-tagged image tag, i.e. a build, not a hash). Current HEAD fixes this:
  `extractBuildSha` pulls the commit sha out of both sides
  (`extractBuildSha('1.0.0-28aac94') => '28aac94'`), so the warning now reads
  *"built from commit fbcf844 but the backend runs commit 28aac94"* — sha-to-sha.
  Both `fbcf8442…` and `28aac94…` are real commits in this repo, so the comparison is
  meaningful. Verified by executing `runnerBuildWarning(liveRunner, '1.0.0-28aac94')`.
  Test `compares a version-tagged backend build sha-to-sha, not hash-to-tag` asserts
  the message matches `/28aac94/` and `not.toMatch(/1\.0\.0-28aac94/)`.
  Additionally, hashes and all-digit build stamps can never parse as versions on
  either side: frontend `versionTuple` rejects `/^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$/i` (mirroring the
  backend `SHA_LIKE_RE`), so `canonicalRunnerVersion('fbcf8442…') === null` and
  `canonicalRunnerVersion('20261117') === null` — verified by execution; a runner
  reporting a hash as its version gets no badge, no warning, no phantom dropdown
  option (test `stays silent when the running version is a build hash, never
  hash-vs-build`).
- **Latest not flagged in the drop-down.** Current `versionSelectorOptions` labels
  every option with `(latest)` / `(running)` flags computed on **canonical** versions,
  and the `Latest` option itself is labelled with the resolved release. Executed with
  the live record: options `[{value:'0.1.0', label:'0.1.0 (latest, running)'}]`,
  `selectedValue 'latest'`, closed select renders `Latest (0.1.0)`. Executed with a
  version-tagged recommended knob (`1.0.0-28aac94`): the dropdown collapses it to one
  canonical row `1.0.0 (latest)` — the raw tag never appears as a phantom option
  (component test `flags the newest release as (latest) even when the recommended
  value is a build tag` asserts exactly
  `['latest=Latest (0.3.0)','0.3.0=0.3.0 (latest)','0.2.0=0.2.0 (running)','0.1.0=0.1.0']`
  and `not.toContain('abc1234')`).

## Goal acceptance (task title + survey)

| Requirement | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Restart as separate destructive action with confirmation window | PASS | `runner-restart-<id>` button (error styling) → `role="alertdialog"` modal naming the runner, "Any work currently running on this runner will be stopped", busy task id shown; backend `requestRestart` in `RUNNER_COMMANDS`, daemon handler writes `restart-requested` sentinel + exit 0, wrapper re-execs same version; old daemons get a disabled button with reason (`canRequestRestart` false for the live 2-command runners — verified by execution) |
| Reload no longer the primary action | PASS | demoted to a text button (`runner-reload-<id>`), still re-reads config |
| Update as separate action | PASS | `runner-update-now-<id>` queues idle-only `requestUpdate` |
| Per-runner version selector, Latest default, pin to a release | PASS | `desiredVersion` in `operatorConfig` (backend backfills `latest`; strict PATCH validation), dropdown PATCHes on change; default latest verified live (`desiredVersion: "latest"` on every runner) |
| Mismatch warning + Update button | PASS | `versionWarningForRunner` fires whenever running ≠ setting (pin or latest); Update installs pin exactly, or recommended when latest |
| Red when a newer version exists | PASS | tier `red` when `known.some(v => running < v)`; soft for pin-older-no-newer; below-minimum always red (verified by execution for pinned-older → red, pinned-newer → red) |
| Auto-update only for Latest, only when idle/restart | PASS | `shouldAutoRequestUpdate` and daemon `maybeSelfUpdate` both gate on `isPinnedDesiredVersion`; pinned runners answer `manual update only` without network |

## Test / lint evidence (run by this review on HEAD `de3b472a`)

- `frontend` full suite: **357 files, 4858 tests, 0 failed** (includes 77
  `runnerConfigHelpers` + 77 `RunnerConfigurationSection` tests).
- `api` flow suite: **112 files, 1576 tests, 0 failed** (includes runnerRegistry,
  runnerRoutes, runnerVersionCompat).
- `runner` `node --test daemon/updates-*`: **203 passed, 0 failed**.
- `eslint` on the two touched frontend files: **0 errors** (21 pre-existing
  `security/detect-object-injection` warnings, same as the rest of the repo).
- `npm run check:binaries` and `check:proof-hygiene`: OK (only known pre-existing
  baseline violations that also exist on origin/main).

## Findings

1. **Must-remove before merge (hygiene, non-feature):** commit `77190e79` added
   `tesseract-0.1.3.tar.gz` (45,555,135 bytes) at the repo root — an accidentally
   downloaded OCR source tarball, tracked by git, unrelated to the feature and not
   covered by `.gitignore`. It does not trip the CI hygiene gates (those cover proof
   images), but it would add 45 MB of junk to main. Fix: `git rm
   tesseract-0.1.3.tar.gz` and add `*.tar.gz` to `.gitignore`. This is stage-harness
   noise, not a defect in the feature code, so it does not fail this stage on its own.
2. **Non-blocking note:** "new version published" resolves to the fleet
   `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` knob (plus fleet-known versions for the red
   tier); publishing without bumping the knob shows no banner. Matches the existing
   publish mechanism (runbook); human reviewers should confirm this is the intended
   release signal.
3. Live runners (`local-alpha`, `local-bravo`, `server2-alpha`) currently advertise
   only `requestModelRediscovery`/`requestUpdate`, so the Restart button correctly
   renders disabled with "too old" guidance until they update — the designed R1
   behaviour, verified against `GET /runners`.

## Verdict

The feature achieves the task goal and the human's ergonomic corrections are verifiably
fixed at HEAD (sha-to-sha build comparison; canonical versions with `(latest)` flags in
the dropdown), with the full frontend/api/runner suites green. Docs (ADR 0012 Amendment
2, `docs/runner-update-runbook.md`) are updated. PASS, with finding 1 as a required
pre-merge cleanup.

/***

 * @description Standalone headless Playwright utility for capturing deterministic
 * screenshots during PR review or verification stages without running ad-hoc background servers.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   node scripts/capture-screenshot.mjs --path "#/tasks/<task-id>"
 *   node scripts/capture-screenshot.mjs --url "http://localhost:3100/#/orchestrator" --out "./docs/tasks/task-1/screenshot.png"
 *   node scripts/capture-screenshot.mjs --path "#/tasks/9940bbbc" --out "./docs/tasks/9940bbbc/stage-review.png"
 *
 * Output default (no --out): resolves the current task id — $TASK_ID, else
 *   $KAINBAIN_TASK_ID, else the kb/<task-id> branch name — and writes to
 *   docs/tasks/<task-id>/screenshot-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>.png (directory created).
 *   An explicit --out always wins. With no discoverable id the script exits
 *   non-zero naming the expected --out form instead of writing to repo root.
 *   A default name already taken by an earlier same-second capture gains a
 *   -01, -02, ... suffix instead of overwriting (explicit --out keeps
 *   today's exact overwrite behavior). A flag token right after --out
 *   counts as a missing value, never as a path.

 *   discoverable, when the id is unsafe for a path, or when all 99

 *   2. Before claiming validity: `xxd -l 8 <out>` (expect `8950 4e47…`)

/***
 * MARK: capture-screenshot.mjs
 * @description Standalone headless Playwright utility for capturing deterministic
 * screenshots during PR review or verification stages without running ad-hoc background servers.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   node scripts/capture-screenshot.mjs --path "#/tasks/<task-id>"
 *   node scripts/capture-screenshot.mjs --url "http://localhost:3100/#/orchestrator" --out "./docs/tasks/task-1/screenshot.png"
 *   node scripts/capture-screenshot.mjs --path "#/tasks/9940bbbc" --out "./docs/tasks/9940bbbc/stage-review.png"

 *   $KAINBAIN_TASK_ID, else the kb/<task-id> branch name — and writes to

 *   non-zero naming the expected --out form instead of writing to repo root.

16|   warning *"This runner was built from fbcf844 but the backend runs 1.0.0-2…"*, and
17|   the closed selector `Latest (0.1.0)` with hint "Tracks the newest release — …".

19|   the working tree) end to end for the touched units:
20|   `frontend/src/components/settings/runnerConfigHelpers.js`,
21|   `RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx`, `api/flow/runnerVersionCompat.js`,
22|   `api/flow/runnerRegistry.js`, `runner/daemon.js`.

24|   (`GET /runners` → `local-alpha`) and the live backend build identity
25|   (`GET /status` → `build.commit = "1.0.0-28aac94"`, image tag

29|## Human correction (assets/19126.png) — verified fixed at HEAD
30|
31|Complaint: *"it's comparing a hash to a build and the latest image seems to not be
32|flagged as latest in the drop-down".*
33|
34|- **Hash vs build.** At screenshot time the sha-mismatch warning printed the raw
35|  backend identity next to the runner hash (`fbcf844` vs `1.0.0-28aac94` — a
36|  version-tagged image tag, i.e. a build, not a hash). Current HEAD fixes this:
37|  `extractBuildSha` pulls the commit sha out of both sides
38|  (`extractBuildSha('1.0.0-28aac94') => '28aac94'`), so the warning now reads
39|  *"built from commit fbcf844 but the backend runs commit 28aac94"* — sha-to-sha.
40|  Both `fbcf8442…` and `28aac94…` are real commits in this repo, so the comparison is
41|  meaningful. Verified by executing `runnerBuildWarning(liveRunner, '1.0.0-28aac94')`.
42|  Test `compares a version-tagged backend build sha-to-sha, not hash-to-tag` asserts
43|  the message matches `/28aac94/` and `not.toMatch(/1\.0\.0-28aac94/)`.
44|  Additionally, hashes and all-digit build stamps can never parse as versions on
45|  either side: frontend `versionTuple` rejects `/^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$/i` (mirroring the
46|  backend `SHA_LIKE_RE`), so `canonicalRunnerVersion('fbcf8442…') === null` and
47|  `canonicalRunnerVersion('20261117') === null` — verified by execution; a runner
48|  reporting a hash as its version gets no badge, no warning, no phantom dropdown
49|  option (test `stays silent when the running version is a build hash, never
50|  hash-vs-build`).
51|- **Latest not flagged in the drop-down.** Current `versionSelectorOptions` labels
52|  every option with `(latest)` / `(running)` flags computed on **canonical** versions,
53|  and the `Latest` option itself is labelled with the resolved release. Executed with
54|  the live record: options `[{value:'0.1.0', label:'0.1.0 (latest, running)'}]`,
55|  `selectedValue 'latest'`, closed select renders `Latest (0.1.0)`. Executed with a
56|  version-tagged recommended knob (`1.0.0-28aac94`): the dropdown collapses it to one
57|  canonical row `1.0.0 (latest)` — the raw tag never appears as a phantom option
58|  (component test `flags the newest release as (latest) even when the recommended
59|  value is a build tag` asserts exactly
60|  `['latest=Latest (0.3.0)','0.3.0=0.3.0 (latest)','0.2.0=0.2.0 (running)','0.1.0=0.1.0']`
61|  and `not.toContain('abc1234')`).
62|
63|## Goal acceptance (task title + survey)
64|
65|| Requirement | Verdict | Evidence |
66||---|---|---|
67|| Restart as separate destructive action with confirmation window | PASS | `runner-restart-<id>` button (error styling) → `role="alertdialog"` modal naming the runner, "Any work currently running on this runner will be stopped", busy task id shown; backend `requestRestart` in `RUNNER_COMMANDS`, daemon handler writes `restart-requested` sentinel + exit 0, wrapper re-execs same version; old daemons get a disabled button with reason (`canRequestRestart` false for the live 2-command runners — verified by execution) |
68|| Reload no longer the primary action | PASS | demoted to a text button (`runner-reload-<id>`), still re-reads config |
69|| Update as separate action | PASS | `runner-update-now-<id>` queues idle-only `requestUpdate` |
70|| Per-runner version selector, Latest default, pin to a release | PASS | `desiredVersion` in `operatorConfig` (backend backfills `latest`; strict PATCH validation), dropdown PATCHes on change; default latest verified live (`desiredVersion: "latest"` on every runner) |
71|| Mismatch warning + Update button | PASS | `versionWarningForRunner` fires whenever running ≠ setting (pin or latest); Update installs pin exactly, or recommended when latest |
72|| Red when a newer version exists | PASS | tier `red` when `known.some(v => running < v)`; soft for pin-older-no-newer; below-minimum always red (verified by execution for pinned-older → red, pinned-newer → red) |
73|| Auto-update only for Latest, only when idle/restart | PASS | `shouldAutoRequestUpdate` and daemon `maybeSelfUpdate` both gate on `isPinnedDesiredVersion`; pinned runners answer `manual update only` without network |
74|

78|  `runnerConfigHelpers` + 77 `RunnerConfigurationSection` tests).
79|- `api` flow suite: **112 files, 1576 tests, 0 failed** (includes runnerRegistry,
80|  runnerRoutes, runnerVersionCompat).
81|- `runner` `node --test daemon/updates-*`: **203 passed, 0 failed**.
82|- `eslint` on the two touched frontend files: **0 errors** (21 pre-existing
83|  `security/detect-object-injection` warnings, same as the rest of the repo).
84|- `npm run check:binaries` and `check:proof-hygiene`: OK (only known pre-existing
85|  baseline violations that also exist on origin/main).
86|

88|
89|1. **Must-remove before merge (hygiene, non-feature):** commit `77190e79` added
90|   `tesseract-0.1.3.tar.gz` (45,555,135 bytes) at the repo root — an accidentally
91|   downloaded OCR source tarball, tracked by git, unrelated to the feature and not
92|   covered by `.gitignore`. It does not trip the CI hygiene gates (those cover proof
93|   images), but it would add 45 MB of junk to main. Fix: `git rm
94|   tesseract-0.1.3.tar.gz` and add `*.tar.gz` to `.gitignore`. This is stage-harness
95|   noise, not a defect in the feature code, so it does not fail this stage on its own.
96|2. **Non-blocking note:** "new version published" resolves to the fleet
97|   `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` knob (plus fleet-known versions for the red
98|   tier); publishing without bumping the knob shows no banner. Matches the existing
99|   publish mechanism (runbook); human reviewers should confirm this is the intended
100|   release signal.

110|the dropdown), with the full frontend/api/runner suites green. Docs (ADR 0012 Amendment
111|2, `docs/runner-update-runbook.md`) are updated. PASS, with finding 1 as a required
112|pre-merge cleanup.

1|# Spike notes — Steps 0a–0c (restart mechanism, version-list source, auto-update matrix)
2|
3|Research for task `78e0522a` (Restart/Update split + per-runner version pinning).
4|Decisions below are as implemented; file/line pointers are to this branch.
5|
6|## 0a — Restart mechanism
7|
8|Question: what does "reboot the runner on its current version" mean mechanically?
9|
10|- Rejected: backend kills the runner remotely (the backend has no shell on
11|  runner hosts — coordination-only, R05 stands), and host-service reboot
12|  (out of scope).
13|- Chosen: a new `requestRestart` backend-to-runner command, symmetric with
14|  `requestUpdate` (`RUNNER_COMMANDS` in `api/flow/runnerRegistry.js`,
15|  consumed in `handlePendingCommands` in `runner/daemon.js`, advertised in
16|  `SUPPORTED_RUNNER_COMMANDS`). It reboots at once — a live execution is
17|  stopped, never drained (survey q2 destructive semantics); the orphaned
18|  claim lease expires so the work re-queues exactly like a crash.
19|- Hook detail found during review: the `kainbain-runner` wrapper only
20|  re-execs when the `current` symlink target changed (a staged update), so
21|  a bare `process.exit(0)` would STOP a same-version runner instead of
22|  rebooting it. The daemon therefore writes a `restart-requested`
23|  sentinel beside the install root (`requestWrapperRestart` in
24|  `runner/updates/state.js`) before exiting 0; the wrapper consumes it and
25|  boots the SAME tree again. Exit 0 + sentinel keeps systemd
26|  `Restart=on-failure` supervision quiet. A stale sentinel (crash between
27|  write and exit) causes at most one extra boot. Unwrapped
28|  (`node main.js`) runners exit without rebooting — documented in
29|  `docs/runner-update-runbook.md`, same class as staged updates there.
30|- No update check is interleaved (Restart ≠ Update, survey q1); the ack is
31|  confirmed with a final heartbeat first so peek-until-ack redelivery
32|  cannot restart-loop the rebooted runner.
33|
34|## 0b — Version-list + desired-version source of truth
35|
36|- `desiredVersion` lives in `operatorConfig` (`'latest'` default,
37|  backfilled for old state; strict PATCH validation — `latest`/null or a
38|  parseable version, else 400 `INVALID_DESIRED_VERSION`).
39|- The Settings dropdown needs no release-catalogue fetch (offline-safe):
40|  `fleetKnownVersions` in `api/flow/runnerVersionCompat.js` unions every
41|  runner-reported version with the recommended/minimum knobs, newest-first,
42|  capped at 30 (same bound as the runner update client). The UI unions
43|  that with running + recommended + the stored pin so the current
44|  selection is always renderable.
45|- The setting rides the heartbeat `update` directive; the daemon reads the
46|  pin via `pinnedDesiredVersion` (fail-open to latest-tracking on old
47|  backends/junk). Fixed pins above recommended are allowed; below minimum
48|  still 409s (floor unchanged) with a distinct "pin cannot clear the
49|  floor" banner + disabled Update.
50|
51|## 0c — Idle-only auto-update vs restart-triggered update (truth table)
52|
53|| Setting | State | Behaviour |
54||---|---|---|
55|| `latest` | idle (incl. after a restart, once idle) | auto-updates (hourly idle check + daily backend nudge); red banner until converged |
56|| `latest` | busy | red banner + Update button; never interrupted |
57|| pinned | any | never automatic (no nudges, no idle installs); manual Update installs exactly the pin when newer, fails loud otherwise |
58|| pinned = running | — | no warning (unless below minimum — the floor always warns red) |
59|
60|- Backend nudge (`shouldAutoRequestUpdate`) and the daemon idle check
61|  (`maybeSelfUpdate`, non-force) both gate on latest-only; force paths
62|  (manual Update, 409 floor) resolve the pin as the check target.
63|- A restart never installs anything by itself; a Latest runner converges
64|  at its next idle check after the reboot.

1|# Upgrade-safety review — Restart / Update split + per-runner desiredVersion
2|
3|**Stage goal:** verify the current change as implemented will not break existing installs on update. If it would, fail the stage (do not fix).
4|
5|**Branch evaluated:** `kb/78e0522a-430d-4659-9e2f-7db6444d13f9` diff `main...HEAD` (33 files, incl. `api/flow/runnerRegistry.js`, `api/flow/runnerVersionCompat.js`, `runner/daemon.js`, `runner/updates/index.js`, `runner/updates/state.js`, `runner/bin/kainbain-runner`, `frontend/src/components/settings/runnerConfigHelpers.js`, `frontend/src/components/settings/RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx`).
6|
7|## Method
8|Read every changed file on `HEAD` against `main`, plus `scripts/lib/runner-install-root.sh`, `scripts/install-local-runner.sh`, `scripts/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.sh`, `scripts/package-runner.mjs`, and the persisted-state loaders (`api/flow/runnerRegistry.js::_loadState`, `runner/updates/state.js::readUpdateState`). Checked both rollout directions: (a) old installs self-updating to the new code, (b) mixed fleet (new backend ↔ old runner, old backend ↔ new runner, new frontend ↔ old backend).
9|
10|## Backward-compatibility properties verified
11|
12|### 1. Backend persisted state — additive, lenient load, no version bump
13|- `RUNNER_STATE_VERSION` stays `3`. `_loadState`/`_persist` call `normalizeOperatorConfig` unconditionally. New field `desiredVersion` defaults to `"latest"` in `defaultOperatorConfig` and is normalized via `normalizeDesiredVersion(raw.desiredVersion ?? "latest")`. Test `old state predating desiredVersion backfills to latest` (`api/flow/runnerRegistry.test.js`) writes a v3 file without the field (operatorConfig `{ displayName: null }`) and asserts both `desiredVersion` and `operatorConfig.desiredVersion` read `"latest"` after load.
14|- `normalizeDesiredVersion` (`api/flow/runnerVersionCompat.js`) is lenient on STORE: `null`/`undefined`/`""`/`"latest"`(any case) → `"latest"`; version-like strings coerce via `coerceRunnerVersion`; anything else falls back to `"latest"` — never stranded on an undeployable value. Strictness lives only on `PATCH` (`updateConfig` throws `400 INVALID_DESIRED_VERSION` for malformed strings/non-strings), so a hand-edited state file cannot brick the registry.
15|- `normalizePendingCommands`/`normalizeCommandResults` filter by `RUNNER_COMMANDS.includes(command)`. Upgrading is safe (old entries are a subset of the new three). Downgrading past a queued `requestRestart` drops that one command — at-most-once semantics, not a fleet brick.
16|- `updateConfig` whitelist adds `"desiredVersion"`; the `next` copy seeds `desiredVersion: current.desiredVersion ?? "latest"` so PATCHes that omit the field (the only shape old frontends send) preserve the setting instead of resetting it.
17|- `_public` is additive: `desiredVersion`, `availableVersions`, `update.desiredVersion` are new keys; no existing key is renamed/removed. `fleetKnownVersions` is pure, offline-safe (unions runner-reported versions + `recommended`/`minimum` knobs, `coerceRunnerVersion`-filtered, capped 30) and cannot throw on junk records.
18|
19|### 2. Old runner ↔ new backend
20|- Old daemon advertises `["requestModelRediscovery","requestUpdate"]` and ignores unknown commands (`handlePendingCommands` `continue`s). New backend's `enqueueCommand` never gates on advertised commands (pre-existing behaviour), but the UI gates on `commands.supported` (`canRequestRestart` in `runnerConfigHelpers.js` requires `requestRestart` in `facts.commands`), so operators see a disabled Restart with "too old — update the Runner" guidance instead of a dead button. A queued `requestRestart` for a pre-feature runner simply sits until TTL (`24h`) and expires as a failed ack — no crash, no workflow interruption, R1 pattern preserved.
21|- `updateDirectiveFromBeat` on old runners returns only three keys; new directive adds `desiredVersion: null`. Old runners ignore the new field (their `updateDirectiveFromBeat` predates it). Compat-gated selection therefore behaves exactly as before.
22|- `shouldAutoRequestUpdate` gains `desiredVersion` param gated by `isPinnedDesiredVersion(desiredVersion ?? DESIRED_VERSION_LATEST)`. Old runners have no pin (default `"latest"`), so the daily auto-nudge behaviour is unchanged: at most one pending, daily cooldown, idle-only apply retained.
23|
24|### 3. New runner ↔ old backend
25|- `updateDirectiveFromBeat` reads `desiredVersion` via `pick(update.desiredVersion)` → `null` when the backend omits it. `pinnedDesiredVersion` maps `null`/`"latest"`(any case)/`""`/non-string/junk → `null` (fail-open to latest-tracking, today's behaviour). `maybeSelfUpdate` only skips auto-checks when `effectiveTarget` is a valid pinned string, so old-backend runners keep the hourly idle check + 409-triggered path unchanged. Verified by `pinnedDesiredVersion` and `maybeSelfUpdate` unit tests (`runner/daemon.test.js`: `pinnedDesiredVersion({ desiredVersion: "bogus" }) => null`; heartbeat cases carry `desiredVersion: null`).
26|- `SUPPORTED_RUNNER_COMMANDS` and `support` filtering are additive. An old backend returns `supported` without `requestRestart` (its `RUNNER_COMMANDS` has two entries), so the new frontend renders Restart disabled — never a broken action.
27|
28|### 4. Runner self-update — default-path unchanged, new path fail-closed and downgrade-proof
29|- `checkForUpdate` gains `targetVersion = null` default. `checkGithubForUpdate`/`checkMirrorForUpdate`/`checkSingleMirrorManifest` take `targetVersion` through and branch only when truthy; when `null` every pre-filter is the old expression (`isNewerVersion`, `isPrereleaseVersion` skip, compat filter). The pinned pre-checks (`isValidVersion`, `compareVersions` order `-1`/`0`/`null`) short-circuit before any network when `targetVersion` is set, so junk pins fail loud (`ok:false`, reason string) and never install.
30|- Pinned install constraints: `compareVersions(target, current) === 0` → `ok:true, update:null, reason:"already on pinned"` (no-op); `-1` → `ok:false, reason:"never downgrades"`; `null` → `ok:false, reason:"cannot compare"`. Mirror/GitHub list walks match `compareVersions(tag, target) === 0` only, never a newer substitute. `checkSingleMirrorManifest` requires the served manifest version to equal the pin. These satisfy ADR 0012 "never downgrade" and "verified, compat-filtered" invariants; a pinned runner therefore cannot silently jump over its pin nor strand below the fleet floor (floor still 409s, UI disables Update with `pinBlocksUpdateReason`).
31|- `maybeSelfUpdate` with a pin and `!force` returns `{ checked:false, reason:"pinned to X: manual update only" }` without touching the network. Manual `requestUpdate` (force) passes the pin through as `targetVersion`. Indistinguishable from the old path when no pin is present.
32|
33|### 5. Same-tree Restart reboot — sentinel is best-effort; shutdown is not breakage
34|- New daemon `requestRestart` handler: stage ack → confirm heartbeat (best-effort, warned on failure) → `requestWrapperRestart({ installRoot: installRootFor(config) })` in try/catch (warns `sentinel not written`) → `process.exit(0)`. The `try/catch` + warn makes an unwritable/missing install root degrade to a plain exit, never a crash. An unwrapped `node main.js` host therefore just exits (as documented) instead of erroring.
35|- Wrapper (`runner/bin/kainbain-runner`) change: only the `AFTER === BEFORE` branch gains `if [ -f "$INSTALL_ROOT/restart-requested" ]; then rm -f …; RESTARTS++; sleep 2; continue; fi`. Normal completion (single-assignment done / idle-out, no sentinel, no `current` flip) still `exit 0`s directly. A staged update still re-execs via the existing `AFTER != BEFORE` branch. Non-zero daemon exits still propagate with no loop. Stale sentinel safety: `rm -f` before re-exec + the shared `RESTARTS > 50` cap guarantees at most one extra boot, never a loop (both covered in `runner/updates-wrapper.test.js`).
36|- `requestWrapperRestart` creates the install root recursively and writes `{ pid, at }` JSON. It does not touch `update-state.json` (`readUpdateState` still reports `"idle"` in tests), so the failed-boot rollback gate (`bootstrapUpdateState`, `MAX_BOOT_ATTEMPTS = 3`) is unaffected. A sentinel left by a crash between write and exit is consumed by the same restart counter, not by the boot-attempt gate.
37|- Existing installs self-updating: `applyUpdate` flips `current`/`previous` and leaves `$INSTALL_ROOT/bin/kainbain-runner` as a stable shim copy. The extracted new tree *contains* the sentinel-aware wrapper but the shim is not refreshed by `applyUpdate`. The old shim still re-execs on `current` flips (old update behaviour intact). The sentinel from the new daemon is ignored by the old shim (no match, plain `exit 0`); systemd units in this repo use `Restart=always` (`scripts/install-local-runner.sh`, `startRunner.sh`), so the reboot strength is unchanged. No install is stranded without a running daemon; the worst case is the new Restart feature degrading to a systemd restart until the shim is re-laid by `install-local-runner`/`migrate-runner-to-wrapper` (both already copy `runner/bin/kainbain-runner` to `$INSTALL_ROOT/bin/kainbain-runner`). This is a feature staleness gap, not a break of existing update/heartbeat/dispatch behaviour.
38|
39|### 6. Frontend / API — dual-read fallbacks, no breaking contract change
40|- `resolveDesiredVersion` falls back `desiredVersion ?? operatorConfig.desiredVersion ?? update.desiredVersion ?? "latest"`; `normalizeDesiredVersion` trims and case-folds. Old backends return `undefined`/`""` for the new keys, which read `"latest"` — the version selector renders "Latest (recommended)" and `versionWarningForRunner` for a latest-runner compares `compareRunnerVersions(running, recommended)`.
41|- `versionOptions` unions `selected.availableVersions ?? []`, `recommendedVersion`, `runningVersion`, and the stored pin, then sorts via `compareRunnerVersions(b, a) ?? 0`, so the current selection is always renderable even when the backend list is empty (offline/regression path). `compareRunnerVersions` returns `null` for unparseable inputs and every caller treats `null` as "cannot prove a difference" — warnings stay quiet on junk instead of scaring.
42|- `Reload` is preserved as a demoted text button (`data-testid=runner-reload-<id>`, `title="Reload configuration from backend"`). *Restart* is a new separate destructive button with `role="alertdialog"` confirmation (`runner-restart-modal-<id>`, names the runner, warns running work will be stopped, shows current task id when busy). Breaking nothing that existed; `reloadSelected` still re-reads config.
43|- `domainRegistry` and `runnerRequests` add one operation (`requestRunnerRestart`, `POST /runners/:id/commands { command: "requestRestart" }`) and no operation is removed/renamed. The previous CI failures (`api.surface.test.js`, `domainRequests.test.js` pinning exact key lists) were updated to include the new key; the full frontend suite passes on this branch.
44|
45|### 7. What was *not* changed
46|- No new required env vars, no config-schema migration, no `RUNNER_STATE_VERSION` bump, no protocol bump (`RUNNER_PROTOCOL = "v1"` unchanged), no `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` / `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` semantics change, no runner-bytes-via-backend (R05 stands; Amendment 2 touches only the *directive*), no Windows/pre-release policy change.
47|- `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js` is untouched by the branch (`git diff` null) — the only backend file in the diff is `api/flow/runnerRegistry.js` plus compat helpers. `runner/updates/state.js` only adds `RESTART_REQUEST_FILE` + `requestWrapperRestart`; `readUpdateState`/`writeUpdateState`/`acquireUpdateLock`/`bootstrapUpdateState` semantics unchanged.
48|
49|## Verdict
50|No clause of the change breaks an existing install on update. Every rollout direction was verified against actual loader/dispatch code and existing tests: old state backfills, old runners ignore or disable the new command, new runners read old directives as latest, pinned installs fail closed without downgrading, and the Restart sentinel degrades to a systemd restart rather than stranding a runner. The sole soft spot — `$INSTALL_ROOT/bin/kainbain-runner` not being refreshed by `applyUpdate` — leaves the reboot strength intact via `Restart=always` and is already the documented shim-refresh path through the installers, not a fleet break.
51|
52|**Gate check (evidence on this branch):**
53|- `api/flow/runnerRegistry.test.js` — backfill, PATCH validation, `requestRestart` enqueue/ack, pinned no-auto-nudge: green
54|- `runner/daemon.test.js` + `runner/updates-check.test.js` + `runner/updates-state.test.js` + `runner/updates-wrapper.test.js` — pinned target, sentinel write/consume, stale-sentinel single boot: green
55|- Frontend `runnerConfigHelpers.test.js` + `RunnerConfigurationSection.test.jsx` — latest default, downgrade guard, red-vs-soft tiers: green
56|- Fast-gate `ci-fast-gate-20261117-035740` — `Unit Tests (api)` failure is the pre-existing flaky `gitGate.test.js` timeout (unrelated to runners; the branch's `gitGate.test.js` change hardens the test, not the product); `Unit Tests (runner)` and `Unit Tests (frontend)` are PASS.
