1|# Implementation plan — Restart and Update as separate runner options + per-runner version pinning
2|
3|## Goal
4|
5|Replace the ambiguous "reload" affordance on the System Settings › Runners screen with two
6|separate actions — **Restart** (destructive, confirmed) and **Update** (reinstall to a
7|different/newer version) — and add per-runner version control: each runner is pinned either
8|to `Latest` (default) or to one fixed release, with a version-mismatch warning and an
9|Update button, red when a newer version exists.
10|
11|Source request: task title + screenshot (`assets/image.png` shows one runner row,
12|`local-alpha`, with PAUSE / REVOKE / RELOAD buttons, a build line, and a yellow
13|version-mismatch banner). Binding survey answers: `SURVEY.md` (round 1, all six questions
14|answered; see §1).
15|
16|## 1. Binding survey decisions (do not re-litigate)
17|
18|| # | Decision |
19||---|---|
20|| q1 | Restart = reboot the runner on its current version (debug use when a runner looks stuck). Update = reinstall it onto a different/newer version. Two separate buttons; RELOAD goes away as a runner action. |
21|| q2 | Restart confirmation warns that any work currently running on that runner will be stopped. |
22|| q3 | Per-runner dropdown: `Latest` plus every released version to pick from. |
23|| q4 | Mismatch warning appears whenever the runner's version differs from its own setting, whether fixed or `Latest`. |
24|| q5 | Automatic update happens only for `Latest` runners, and only when the runner next restarts or is idle with no work running (no mid-work interruption). |
25|| q6 | Red warning when a newer version exists than the one the runner is on; softer colour for other mismatches. |
26|
27|Notes captured: restart is a debug tool for stuck runners (q1); Latest default per the
28|original request.
29|
30|## 2. Current-state map (verified in repo)
31|
32|- UI: [RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx](/frontend/src/components/settings/RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx) — detail panel with lifecycle controls, `reloadSelected` (re-reads config from backend, §335–358 — this is the "RELOAD" the screenshot shows; it does **not** touch the runner process), `handleUpdateNow` → `api.requestRunnerUpdate` (queues idle-only `requestUpdate`, §654–676).
33|- Helpers: [runnerConfigHelpers.js](/frontend/src/components/settings/runnerConfigHelpers.js) — `runRunnerAction` (approve/deny/pause/resume/revoke only, §143–150), `canRequestUpdate`/`canRequestRediscovery` (§421–437), `describeRunnerVersion` (§162–168), `describeRunnerBuild` + `runnerBuildWarning` (§735–810, stale-code banner that already says "restart or update it").
34|- API surface: [frontend/src/services/runners/index.js](/frontend/src/services/runners/index.js) — `requestRunnerUpdate` posts `{ command: 'requestUpdate' }` to `/runners/:id/commands`; no restart endpoint exists.
35|- Backend: [api/flow/runnerRegistry.js](/api/flow/runnerRegistry.js) — `RUNNER_COMMANDS = ["requestModelRediscovery", "requestUpdate"]` (§179); heartbeat auto-nudge queues `requestUpdate` for runners trailing recommended version, max one pending and daily per runner (Amendment 1 of [ADR 0012](/docs/adr/0012-runner-artifact-update-channel.md)).
36|- Runner: [runner/daemon.js](/runner/daemon.js) consumes backend-to-runner commands, advertises `SUPPORTED_RUNNER_COMMANDS` in facts; updates apply idle-only via [runner/updates/](/runner/updates/index.js) (download → verify against pinned key → atomic symlink flip, never downgrade). No restart command exists anywhere.
37|- Update policy source of truth: `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` / `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` env knobs; procedures in [docs/runner-update-runbook.md](/docs/runner-update-runbook.md). ADR 0012 explicitly deferred per-runner pinning ("no per-runner pinning" in survey refinements) — this task reverses that for the *desired-version* directive only (backend still never serves bytes; R05 stands).
38|- Tests: `frontend/src/components/settings/runnerConfigHelpers.test.js`, `RunnerConfigurationSection.test.jsx`, `api/flow/runnerVersionCompat.test.js`, `runner/updates-*.test.js`, `api/flow/runnerRoutes.test.js`.
39|
40|## 3. Approach — make the change easy, then make the change
41|
42|Do the work in this order so each step is independently shippable and the hard
43|research lands first:
44|
45|1. **Research spikes first** (Steps 0a–0c): restart mechanism, version-list source, desired-version storage. These answer the only unknowns; everything after is mechanical.
46|2. **Make the change easy**: extract the runner-action button + status-line block in `RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx` into small components/helpers with unit tests, so adding Restart/Update/version-selector is adding props, not rewriting the panel.
47|3. **Make the change**: backend `requestRestart` command + desired-version field, runner daemon support, then UI (separate buttons, confirm modal, version dropdown, warning tiers).
48|4. **Assure it**: unit/integration/e2e per step + docs updates; keep the old behaviour green until the new one lands.
49|
50|Non-goals: backend serving runner bytes (R05 stands); Windows support; pre-release opt-in; changing 409/minimum-floor semantics; touching pause/resume/revoke.
51|
52|## 4. Step-by-step plan
53|
54|### Step 0a — Spike: restart mechanism (do first; biggest unknown)
55|
56|- Question: what does "reboot the runner on its current version" mean mechanically? Candidates: (a) new `requestRestart` backend-to-runner command consumed by the daemon (graceful: finish-or-kill work, re-exec wrapper `current` without version change); (b) backend kills the runner process remotely (no — backend has no shell on runner hosts); (c) restart = re-register/reboot host service (out of scope).
57|- Investigate: how the daemon loop in [runner/daemon.js](/runner/daemon.js) consumes `requestUpdate` end-to-end (heartbeat → ack → idle-apply), where a restart hook fits, what "stop running work" means for claimed tasks (requeue vs kill), and how the wrapper (`bin/kainbain-runner`) re-execs `current`.
58|- Decide: recommended (a) — symmetric with `requestUpdate`, honours the q2 destructive semantics (work is stopped, not drained), keeps backend coordination-only.
59|- Evidence: spike note (≤1 page) in the task docs folder naming the chosen hook point and the work-stop semantics.
60|
61|### Step 0b — Spike: version-list + desired-version source of truth
62|
63|- Questions: where does the per-runner dropdown's release list come from? Where is `desiredVersion` (`latest` | semver) stored?
64|- Investigate: backend registry record shape + persistence (disk vs memory — note `pendingCommands` are memory-only per `runnerRegistry.js` §160); whether the backend can list GitHub releases server-side or should expose `recommendedVersion` + a cached release index; how `operatorConfig` (already PATCH-able per runner) could carry `desiredVersion` with `latest` default and backfill for old records.
65|- Recommended direction (to confirm in spike): `desiredVersion` lives in `operatorConfig` (`null`/`"latest"` = Latest, default); dropdown options = cached release list endpoint (newest-first, same 30-entry bound as the runner client) falling back to `{ current, recommended }` when offline; fixed pin = exact semver; runners resolve `latest` → newest compatible release via the existing compat filter.
66|- Evidence: spike note + decision on storage/endpoint shape before any schema change.
67|
68|### Step 0c — Spike: idle-only auto-update vs restart-triggered update
69|
70|- Reconcile q5 ("only when the runner next restarts or is sitting idle") with current behaviour (hourly idle check + 409-triggered + daily auto-nudge for trailers). Decide the exact matrix: Latest+idle → auto; Latest+busy → wait; fixed-pin → never auto (manual Update only); restart of a Latest runner → check-and-update on boot before claiming work.
71|- Evidence: one truth-table in the spike note; it becomes the acceptance table in §6.
72|
73|### Step 1 — Test-seam refactor (make the change easy)
74|
75|- Extract from `RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx`: action-button row (with disabled-reason tooltips), command status-line builder, version/warning banner block into testable units beside `runnerConfigHelpers.js`.
76|- Add missing unit coverage for current behaviour first (`runRunnerAction` unknown-action null, `canRequestUpdate` gating, `runnerBuildWarning` branches) so refactors are provably safe.
77|- Gate: `npm run test:unit` + existing `RunnerConfigurationSection.test.jsx` green, no visual change.
78|
79|### Step 2 — Backend: `requestRestart` command (mirror `requestUpdate`)
80|
81|- Add `requestRestart` to `RUNNER_COMMANDS` in `api/flow/runnerRegistry.js`, queue/dedupe/cooldown semantics (mirror `requestUpdate`; decide cooldown in Step 0a), `POST /runners/:id/commands { command: 'requestRestart' }` path, `runnerApi.requestRunnerRestart` in `frontend/src/services/runners/index.js`, `runRunnerAction`-adjacent dispatcher entry.
82|- Gate: `api/flow/runnerRoutes.test.js` + registry unit tests for queue/dedupe.
83|
84|### Step 3 — Runner daemon: consume `requestRestart`
85|
86|- Advertise support in `SUPPORTED_RUNNER_COMMANDS`; implement restart: stop in-flight work per Step 0a semantics (heartbeat ack carries what was stopped), re-exec wrapper on the **same** version (no update check interleaved — Restart ≠ Update per q1), re-register.
87|- Safety: restart never triggers an update on a fixed-pin runner; on a Latest runner it may check-and-update on boot per Step 0c matrix (document which).
88|- Gate: `runner/daemon.test.js` + idle/busy restart cases; chaos coverage per `docs/manual-testing/09-runner-chaos.md`.
89|
90|### Step 4 — Backend + registry: `desiredVersion` per runner
91|
92|- Schema per Step 0b (`operatorConfig.desiredVersion`, default Latest, backfill old/empty → Latest); PATCH validation (exact semver from release list or `latest`); include resolved `desired` + `latest` + release list in `GET /runners` records (or a lightweight releases endpoint); keep env knobs as fleet defaults.
93|- Decide conflict rule: fixed pin above recommended is allowed (asymmetric updates already accepted per ADR Amendment 1); fixed pin below minimum still 409s (floor unchanged).
94|- Gate: registry + compat tests (`runnerVersionCompat.test.js`).
95|
96|### Step 5 — UI: separate Restart / Update, confirm modal, version selector, warning tiers
97|
98|- Replace RELOAD-as-action with: **Restart** (destructive styling, opens confirm modal with q2 copy: names the runner, warns running work will be stopped, requires explicit confirm; disabled with reason when runner not active/old) and **Update** (queues reinstall to resolved target: fixed pin → that version; Latest → newest compatible; shows target version in tooltip as today).
99|- Keep config re-read available but demote it (e.g. small refresh icon, not a primary button) so no capability is lost.
100|- Per-runner version dropdown (`Latest` + releases, default Latest) bound to `desiredVersion` PATCH.
101|- Warning logic per q4/q6: mismatch(runnerVersion vs resolved desired) → banner + Update button; tier = red when a newer version exists than running (scare), softer otherwise (e.g. pinned older-behind, dev checkout, unknown). Preserve `runnerBuildWarning` sha-mismatch branch or merge it into the same banner (decide in implementation; no double banners).
102|- Distinguish three states explicitly: update queued/pending, last-update failed (with reason), update available — reusing the existing `commands.pending`/`results` + `updateStatus` plumbing.
103|- Gate: helper unit tests (warning-tier matrix) + `RunnerConfigurationSection.test.jsx` additions + headless screenshot (`npm run capture:screenshot`) of row states.
104|
105|### Step 6 — Auto-update behaviour for Latest (q5)
106|
107|- Implement the Step 0c matrix; default Latest for new runners; no auto-update for fixed pins (manual Update only).
108|- Gate: daemon update-client tests + heartbeat-nudge tests proving busy runners are never interrupted.
109|
110|### Step 7 — Docs + runbook
111|
112|- Update [docs/runner-update-runbook.md](/docs/runner-update-runbook.md) (Restart vs Update, pin procedure, Latest auto behaviour, triage for the new banners), the Runners settings UI copy, and ADR 0012 Amendment 2 (per-runner desired-version reverses the "no per-runner pinning" deferral for selection only).
113|- Backwards-compat note: old runners (no `requestRestart`, no `desiredVersion`) show disabled buttons + "update the runner to enable this" guidance, mirroring the existing R1 pattern.
114|
115|## 5. Ordering / dependencies
116|
117|`0a, 0b, 0c` (any order, all before schema) → `1` → `2 → 3` (backend then daemon; UI Restart in 5 may mock until 3 lands) → `4` → `5` → `6` → `7`. Steps 2–3 and 4 are parallelisable once spikes conclude.
118|
119|## 6. Acceptance table (from survey; verify every row)
120|
121|| Runner setting | Runner state | Expected |
122||---|---|---|
123|| any | press Restart | confirm modal (q2 copy) → reboot same version, running work stopped |
124|| fixed pin = running | — | no warning |
125|| fixed pin ≠ running | — | softer warning + Update → reinstalls pinned version |
126|| Latest, running = newest | — | no warning |
127|| Latest, trailing | idle/restart | auto-updates (q5); banner red until converged (q6) |
128|| Latest, trailing | busy | red banner + Update button; no interruption |
129|| any old runner | — | disabled controls + "too old" guidance, never a dead button |
130|
131|## 7. Assurance plan (how we prove it)
132|
133|- Unit: `npm run test:unit` — new helper tests (restart dispatcher, desired-version normalisation, warning-tier matrix incl. red-vs-soft), registry queue/dedupe/cooldown tests, daemon command tests.
134|- Integration: runner update-client + heartbeat suites (`runner/updates-*.test.js`, daemon tests) for idle-only apply, never-downgrade, opt-out ack, fixed-pin-no-auto.
135|- UI: extend `RunnerConfigurationSection.test.jsx` (two buttons, modal copy, dropdown default Latest, banner tiers); headless capture (`npm run capture:screenshot`) of: clean row, soft mismatch, red newer-available, pending-update, failed-update, confirm modal.
136|- Manual: runbook triage walkthrough (stale runner, failed update, old runner) + chaos checklist (`docs/manual-testing/09-runner-chaos.md`).
137|- Docs: runbook + ADR amendment + settings copy reviewed in the same PR; no code lands without its docs row in §6 re-verified.
138|- Regression: full suite for touched packages; `api/flow/runnerRoutes.test.js` and existing update-channel tests must stay green (old behaviour preserved until new lands).
139|
140|## 8. Risks
141|
142|- Restart-during-work data loss → mitigated by q2 confirm copy + ack reporting what was stopped; never auto-restart busy runners.
143|- Fixed pin below minimum → 409 loop; UI must surface "pin is below fleet minimum" distinctly from "update available".
144|- Release-list availability offline → dropdown degrades to current+recommended (R03 offline updates keep working).
145|- Scope creep into serving bytes or changing floors → explicitly out; R05 stands.

## Draft 1 — Soften exact-surface API pinning tests so additive operations don't fail CI

- `title`: "Soften exact-surface API pinning tests so additive operations don't fail CI"
- `idempotencyKey`: `b7c2da50090f4a6cfa63dd3f810057d9`
- Dedupe keywords: surface pin, api.surface, domainRequests, exact keys

`goal`:

Two frontend tests assert the ENTIRE API key list with `toEqual`:
`frontend/src/services/api.surface.test.js` ("exposes the pinned non-domain
keys plus exactly the registry operations", line 17) and
`frontend/src/services/domainRequests.test.js` ("exposes exactly the registry
operations with no duplicates", line 16). Their purpose is to catch dropped
or renamed operations, but as written they also fail on purely ADDITIVE
changes: adding one new operation (`requestRunnerRestart`) failed the full
gate (`Unit Tests (frontend)`, 2 failed / 4805 passed) and cost a whole
~14-minute CI cycle plus an agent fix-and-retry loop for a change that broke
nothing. Change both tests to fail on removed/renamed keys while passing (or
explicitly warning) on added keys — e.g. assert the expected set is a subset
of the actual keys and report additions separately — or generate the expected
list from the operation registry so additive changes stay green by
construction. Keep the dropped-operation detection: removing an operation
must still fail loudly. Verify by adding a dummy operation and showing the
suite stays green, then removing one and showing it fails.

Case-study reference: task `78e0522a-430d-4659-9e2f-7db6444d13f9`
(Restart/Update runner split),
`docs/tasks/78e0522a-430d-4659-9e2f-7db6444d13f9/automated-tests-failure-20261117-010944.md`
and `ci-fast-gate-20261117-010508/unit-tests-frontend.full.log`.

---

## Draft 2 — Cut the gitGate test's 15-minute starvation budget and quarantine the flake

- `title`: "Cut the gitGate test's 15-minute starvation budget and quarantine the flake"
- `idempotencyKey`: `8c78625b0884a5572e5a8c14c501f5a0`
- Dedupe keywords: gitGate, starvation, flake, timeout

`goal`:

`api/gitGate.test.js` sets `STARVATION_BUDGET_MS = 900000` (15 minutes) as
the `it` timeout for the git serialization tests. When the "never runs two
git processes on the same repo at once" test flaked, it hung the entire
`Unit Tests (api)` branch for 1057s and failed the whole gate on code
completely unrelated to the change under test — roughly 17 minutes of dead
agent iteration time per occurrence. A prior test-only hardening
(`0603447d`) reduced the odds but the 15-minute budget is still in place, so
the next hang costs the same. Reduce the budget to a tight value that still
distinguishes real serialization regressions from slowness (tens of seconds,
not minutes), make the test self-diagnose on timeout (log which promise
never settled instead of a bare timeout), and consider moving this
timing-sensitive test out of the blocking fast gate into a non-blocking lane
so one flaky timing test can never again hold 7400 passing tests hostage.
Verify with repeated runs and by showing a forced-hang fails fast with a
useful message.

Case-study reference: task `78e0522a-430d-4659-9e2f-7db6444d13f9`
(Restart/Update runner split),
`docs/tasks/78e0522a-430d-4659-9e2f-7db6444d13f9/automated-test-2-failure-20261117-041518.md`
and `ci-fast-gate-20261117-035740/unit-tests-api.full.log`.

---

## Draft 3 — Unify runner/backend build identity into one canonical contract

- `title`: "Unify runner/backend build identity into one canonical contract"
- `idempotencyKey`: `4a12ba7d12d46c2abc4c6e50287ff500`
- Dedupe keywords: build identity, version compare, canonical version, hash vs build

`goal`:

Runner version identity currently lives in three-plus independent
implementations: `api/flow/runnerVersionCompat.js` (backend semver),
`frontend/src/components/settings/runnerConfigHelpers.js` (frontend numeric
compare + `SHA_LIKE_RE`), and `runner/updates/index.js` /
`runner/updates/manifest.js` (update client). They already diverged once in
production: the Runners settings UI compared a runner build hash (`fbcf844`)
against a version-tagged backend image tag (`1.0.0-28aac94`) — a hash vs a
build — and mis-flagged which release was latest in the version dropdown,
which a human reviewer rejected with a screenshot. The fix (`extractBuildSha`,
`canonicalRunnerVersion`, mirrored sha-regex guards) had to be hand-applied
in each layer and can drift again with the next edit. Define ONE canonical
build-identity contract (what a version is, what a build/commit is, how
`1.0.0-28aac94`-style tags canonicalize, what never parses as a version)
plus a shared conformance fixture covering mixed identities (plain semver,
short/long hashes, tagged builds, numeric stamps, junk), and make every
layer implement or import it with tests asserting identical verdicts on the
fixture. No layer may compare raw identity strings across domains again.

Case-study reference: task `78e0522a-430d-4659-9e2f-7db6444d13f9`
(Restart/Update runner split), human rejection in
`docs/tasks/78e0522a-430d-4659-9e2f-7db6444d13f9/final-review-20261117-073507.md`
with `assets/19126.png`, resolved in `stage-review-20261117-092404.md`.

## Draft 4 — Couple release publishing to the recommended-version knob

- `title`: "Couple release publishing to the recommended-version knob"
- `idempotencyKey`: `45ea3efad22dd3ffee67b70aae4192e9`
- Dedupe keywords: recommended version, publish, release knob

`goal`:

The "a new version is published" signal that drives Latest-runner banners and
auto-update is the manually-bumped `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION`
environment knob (`docs/runner-update-runbook.md`, step 5). Publishing a
release WITHOUT bumping the knob shows no banner and triggers no auto-update
— silently defeating the exact UX the version-control feature was built for —
and nothing warns the publisher. Three separate reviews on the same task
flagged this as "human reviewers should confirm", which is process fragility,
not a decision. Make it structural: either the release/publish script bumps
the knob atomically as part of publishing, or a check fails (loudly, at
publish time or in CI) when a release exists that no knob points at.
Document the single publish path in the runbook and remove the manual step.
Verify by publishing a test release and showing the banner/auto-update path
activates with no extra manual action.

Case-study reference: task `78e0522a-430d-4659-9e2f-7db6444d13f9`
(Restart/Update runner split), noted in `pr-review-20261117.md`,
`upgrade-safety-review-20261117.md`, and `stage-review-20261117-092404.md`
(finding 2).

---

## Draft 5 — Extend the binary guard to large non-proof files and ignore archives

- `title`: "Extend the binary guard to large non-proof files and ignore archives"
- `idempotencyKey`: `56a55e5d7dae691a97736eb5d4bb9681`
- Dedupe keywords: binary guard, tarball, gitignore, large file

`goal`:

Agent tooling downloaded `tesseract-0.1.3.tar.gz` (45,555,135 bytes) to the
repo root and it got COMMITTED and tracked (visible in `git ls-files`),
alongside a second tracked archive (`opencode-ai-sdk-1.18.34.tgz`).
`.gitignore` contains no `*.tar.gz`/`*.tgz` entry, and

## Draft 1 — Soften exact-surface API pinning tests so additive operations don't fail CI

- `title`: "Soften exact-surface API pinning tests so additive operations don't fail CI"
- `idempotencyKey`: `b7c2da50090f4a6cfa63dd3f810057d9`
- Dedupe keywords: surface pin, api.surface, domainRequests, exact keys

`goal`:

Two frontend tests assert the ENTIRE API key list with `toEqual`:
`frontend/src/services/api.surface.test.js` ("exposes the pinned non-domain
keys plus exactly the registry operations", line 17) and
`frontend/src/services/domainRequests.test.js` ("exposes exactly the registry
operations with no duplicates", line 16). Their purpose is to catch dropped
or renamed operations, but as written they also fail on purely ADDITIVE
changes: adding one new operation (`requestRunnerRestart`) failed the full
gate (`Unit Tests (frontend)`, 2 failed / 4805 passed) and cost a whole
~14-minute CI cycle plus an agent fix-and-retry loop for a change that broke
nothing. Change both tests to fail on removed/renamed keys while passing (or
explicitly warning) on added keys — e.g. assert the expected set is a subset
of the actual keys and report additions separately — or generate the expected
list from the operation registry so additive changes stay green by
construction. Keep the dropped-operation detection: removing an operation
must still fail loudly. Verify by adding a dummy operation and showing the
suite stays green, then removing one and showing it fails.

## Draft 2 — Cut the gitGate test's 15-minute starvation budget and quarantine the flake

- `title`: "Cut the gitGate test's 15-minute starvation budget and quarantine the flake"
- `idempotencyKey`: `8c78625b0884a5572e5a8c14c501f5a0`
- Dedupe keywords: gitGate, starvation, flake, timeout

`goal`:

`api/gitGate.test.js` sets `STARVATION_BUDGET_MS = 900000` (15 minutes) as
the `it` timeout for the git serialization tests. When the "never runs two
git processes on the same repo at once" test flaked, it hung the entire
`Unit Tests (api)` branch for 1057s and failed the whole gate on code
completely unrelated to the change under test — roughly 17 minutes of dead
agent iteration time per occurrence. A prior test-only hardening
(`0603447d`) reduced the odds but the 15-minute budget is still in place, so
the next hang costs the same. Reduce the budget to a tight value that still
distinguishes real serialization regressions from slowness (tens of seconds,
not minutes), make the test self-diagnose on timeout (log which promise
never settled instead of a bare timeout), and consider moving this
timing-sensitive test out of the blocking fast gate into a non-blocking lane
so one flaky timing test can never again hold 7400 passing tests hostage.
Verify with repeated runs and by showing a forced-hang fails fast with a
useful message.

(Restart/Update runner split),
`docs/tasks/78e0522a-430d-4659-9e2f-7db6444d13f9/automated-test-2-failure-20261117-041518.md`
and `ci-fast-gate-20261117-035740/unit-tests-api.full.log`.

## Draft 3 — Unify runner/backend build identity into one canonical contract

- `title`: "Unify runner/backend build identity into one canonical contract"
- `idempotencyKey`: `4a12ba7d12d46c2abc4c6e50287ff500`
- Dedupe keywords: build identity, version compare, canonical version, hash vs build

`goal`:

Runner version identity currently lives in three-plus independent
implementations: `api/flow/runnerVersionCompat.js` (backend semver),
`frontend/src/components/settings/runnerConfigHelpers.js` (frontend numeric
compare + `SHA_LIKE_RE`), and `runner/updates/index.js` /
`runner/updates/manifest.js` (update client). They already diverged once in
production: the Runners settings UI compared a runner build hash (`fbcf844`)
against a version-tagged backend image tag (`1.0.0-28aac94`) — a hash vs a
build — and mis-flagged which release was latest in the version dropdown,
which a human reviewer rejected with a screenshot. The fix (`extractBuildSha`,
`canonicalRunnerVersion`, mirrored sha-regex guards) had to be hand-applied
in each layer and can drift again with the next edit. Define ONE canonical
build-identity contract (what a version is, what a build/commit is, how
`1.0.0-28aac94`-style tags canonicalize, what never parses as a version)
plus a shared conformance fixture covering mixed identities (plain semver,
short/long hashes, tagged builds, numeric stamps, junk), and make every
layer implement or import it with tests asserting identical verdicts on the
fixture. No layer may compare raw identity strings across domains again.

Case-study reference: task `78e0522a-430d-4659-9e2f-7db6444d13f9`
(Restart/Update runner split), human rejection in
`docs/tasks/78e0522a-430d-4659-9e2f-7db6444d13f9/final-review-20261117-073507.md`
with `assets/19126.png`, resolved in `stage-review-20261117-092404.md`.

## Draft 4 — Couple release publishing to the recommended-version knob

- `title`: "Couple release publishing to the recommended-version knob"
- `idempotencyKey`: `45ea3efad22dd3ffee67b70aae4192e9`
- Dedupe keywords: recommended version, publish, release knob

`goal`:

The "a new version is published" signal that drives Latest-runner banners and
auto-update is the manually-bumped `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION`
environment knob (`docs/runner-update-runbook.md`, step 5). Publishing a
release WITHOUT bumping the knob shows no banner and triggers no auto-update
— silently defeating the exact UX the version-control feature was built for —
and nothing warns the publisher. Three separate reviews on the same task
flagged this as "human reviewers should confirm", which is process fragility,
not a decision. Make it structural: either the release/publish script bumps
the knob atomically as part of publishing, or a check fails (loudly, at
publish time or in CI) when a release exists that no knob points at.
Document the single publish path in the runbook and remove the manual step.
Verify by publishing a test release and showing the banner/auto-update path
activates with no extra manual action.

(Restart/Update runner split), noted in `pr-review-20261117.md`,
`upgrade-safety-review-20261117.md`, and `stage-review-20261117-092404.md`
